results.caption: Honestly not bad.  Pretty chill zone 1 workout just insanely long.  Here’s the full story.  Do you think @Chris C needs to come to Mallorca?  Never swam more than 100 yards. Never biked more than 5 miles. Ran a couple marathons years ago and that’s it. Carb loading the day before did not go well. Basically no breakfast, pancakes for lunch, pasta for dinner, almost a gallon of apple juice. Ended up feeling sick most of the night and barely slept. Woke up rough and still got moving anyway. It’s not a hard day physically, it’s just really long and really boring. I was live on Instagram almost the entire time, which is also why my phone survived since I couldn’t charge it while running.  The only logistical way to fit a run, bike, and swim into one day was to do it in and around my apartment complex. Paced it close to the cutoff times on purpose. Could’ve gone faster but didn’t want to burn out. Did it anyway. Turns out it’s not hard, it’s just really long and really boring. #ironman #ironmantraining #ironmantriathlon #fullironman

results.caption: The Nude Beaches of South Landes (🇫🇷 France) The south Landes coast in southwest France has six nude beaches spread across roughly 70 to 100 kilometres of Atlantic coastline, running from Plage d'Ondres near Biarritz north to Arnaoutchot near Vieux-Boucau. Outside the lifeguarded flags, nudity is broadly accepted on Landes beaches, and this stretch includes the department's only two officially recognized nude beaches: Plage des Culs-Nus in Hossegor and the beach behind the Arnaoutchot naturist resort. Every beach shares the same golden sand and dune backdrop, but each has its own personality, from a pink-painted bunker at Plage des Casernes to hand-carved shell art marking the nude section at Plage des Sablères.   Expect wide, uncrowded sand even in high season, wild Atlantic surf that draws serious surfers to Casernes and Culs-Nus, and pine-forest access roads that dead-end straight at the dunes. Ondres and Sablères sit near lively beach towns with bars and shops, while Casernes and Messanges North stay quiet and remote. Arnaoutchot flips the script entirely: naked is the norm, not the exception, thanks to the resort right behind the beach. If you're a longtime naturist scouting new coastline or planning your first clothing-optional beach trip in France, this guide covers what each Landes nude beach looks like, how to find the unofficial zones, and what makes each one worth the stop. #clothesfree #destinationclothesfree #clothesfreevacations #clothesfreetravel #naturist #travelvibes #tiktoktravel #nudebeach #hiddenparadise #nudistbeach #bucketlist #vacationgoals #france #arna #arnaoutchot

results.caption:
The Best Running Gear in 2026 (in my opinion)

#running #runner #marathon #marathontraining #recommendations
results.profileBio:
I love running and making videos about running
@bpnsupps athlete
results.transcript: This is all the best running gear you can buy in 2026. So many different brands make great running gear, but here are the things I actually use and recommend as a runner. All right, sunglasses. I recommend the Oakley Radar EVs. These look awesome. They're super comfortable and they don't bounce when you're running. I also recommend the Oakley eye jackets. Same thing. They fit super comfortable on your face. A more affordable option that looks similar are the Rendezvous R3s. Good running headphones are super important to me. The Beats Powerbeats Pro 2s have the all-around best fit and sound quality. I've also been loving the Shox Open Dots. Not quite as good sound quality, but still really good. The Shox Open Run Pro 2s are great if you want to feel more aware and have more of an open ear feel. The DSG Quarter Crew socks have and probably always will be my favorite running socks. Then in second place come the Nike Unicorn socks. All right, now the fun stuff, shoes. I have tested all of these extensively. Here are my recommendations. For an affordable daily trainer, New Balance Ellipse. Another well-priced daily trainer are the Adidas Evo SL. My favorite daily trainer to date are the Nike Vomero Plus. For race day or workout shoes, Nike Alpha Fly 3s, Hoka CLO 3s, Adidas Adios Pro 4s, which are probably my favorite race day shoes. And then finally, Saucony Endorphin Elite 3s. If you're a shorts person, my favorite are the Satisfy Spaceo shorts, but they're really expensive. A more affordable option are the New Balance RC shorts. Lululemon Fast and Free shorts are good. And then of course, Nike Trail. I mostly wear half tights. The ones I recommend most are the Lululemon Fast and Free. These will genuinely change your life. Pretty much every brand makes a good running shirt. Just make sure it's lightweight and breathable. My favorite shirts are definitely Satisfy, but they're very expensive. If you're feeling bold, the Nike Radical Airflow shirt is pretty crazy. The two hats I recommend are the CLA hats and the Aloe hats. The CLA 5 panel hat is very flexible and comfortable. And same thing with the Aloe Performance hat. I love this thing. The watch I use is the Garmin 4Runner 970. If you want a more affordable option, use the Coro Space Pro. I wear the Whoop 5.0. I can't sleep with my Garmin, but I can sleep with my Whoop, and it tracks everything I do 24-7. My most essential running supplements are BPN Go gels and BPN electrolytes. And then lastly, for recovery, I recommend the Norma Tech boots.
